researchQuestion: Close the active-batch gate for fully diluted share-count roll-forward and sharpen customer concentration/end-customer mapping from current primary filings.
exactUnresolvedGate: true end-customer mapping, governance and fully diluted share-count roll-forward remain
summary: Primary Q2 2026 filing materially closes the fully diluted denominator mechanics but not true end-customer identity. As of June 30, 2026 Astera had 9.180M RSUs and 0.375M PSUs outstanding, 1.663M customer-warrant shares vested/exercisable plus 0.025M probable to vest, and 10.962M potentially dilutive equivalent shares in Q2 EPS, producing 183.340M diluted weighted-average shares versus 172.378M basic. Customer concentration is extreme and independently quantified, but the filing anonymizes customers A-D, so end-customer identity must remain unknown absent corroborated primary mapping.

evidence.fact: Q2 2026 weighted-average shares were 172.378M basic and 183.340M diluted; potentially dilutive equivalents contributed 10.962M shares.
evidence.sourceLocation: Net income per common share table, filing lines 939-953

evidence.fact: Outstanding equity awards at June 30, 2026 included 9.180M RSUs and 0.375M PSUs; unrecognized RSU compensation was $640.1M and PSU compensation $40.3M.
Customer warrants had 1.663M shares vested/exercisable and 0.025M additional shares probable to vest at June 30, 2026; none had been exercised by the holder as of that date.
Revenue concentration for Q2 2026 was Customer A 29%, B 25%, C 15%, D 13%; for first-half 2026 A 29%, B 21%, C 17%, D 13%.

inference: For underwriting normalization, 183.340M diluted weighted-average shares is the cleanest current GAAP denominator anchor for Q2 earnings analysis, but it is not identical to a point-in-time fully diluted ownership count.

The visible 9.180M RSUs + 0.375M PSUs + approximately 1.688M vested/probable customer-warrant shares explain a large portion of dilution overhang, but option details and treasury-stock-method effects must still be reconciled before Chief labels a point-in-time fully diluted count final.
Customer concentration risk is unquestionably material; however, mapping anonymous A-D to named hyperscalers would be inference unless a primary source explicitly identifies them.
unknowns: Exact named identity of Customers A-D remains undisclosed in the 10-Q.
Point-in-time fully diluted share count still requires reconciliation of options/award treasury-stock-method effects rather than simple summation.
Governance blocker is not addressed by this artifact and should remain open.
falsifiers: A later primary filing showing materially different outstanding award or warrant counts before Chief promotion.
A primary customer disclosure contradicting any inferred hyperscaler mapping.
